objective: Fix the published v0.3.0 default npm-install peer dependency failure, add a regression gate for normal npm resolution, and prepare a non-published v0.3.1 release candidate.
context: GitHub issue #43 tracks this remediation. v0.3.0 is already public on npm with dist-tags.latest=0.3.0 and annotated tag v0.3.0 correctly targets e20f392a8babdaa4d37ffe3239ab3f8885a4a369. Post-publish validation found that a fresh default npm install of @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.0 fails with ERESOLVE in the DSH peer graph while --legacy-peer-deps succeeds. GitHub Release v0.3.0 is still absent, but this task prioritizes correcting the install contract. Prepare v0.3.1 only; do not publish, tag, alter dist-tags, or create a GitHub Release.
forbidden_changes: npm publish, npm unpublish, npm deprecate, npm dist-tag mutation, or any registry mutation
creation, deletion, movement, rewrite, or force-push of any git tag including v0.3.0 or v0.3.1
GitHub Release creation, deletion, publication, or mutation
changes to the already-public v0.3.0 package or tag
using --legacy-peer-deps, --force, --omit=peer, or equivalent resolver bypasses to make the acceptance smoke pass
unrelated runtime behavior changes outside the minimal package/dependency compatibility fix
the user's normal ~/.dsh, official DSH web profile, credential stores, provider key files, or other secrets
validation: Validate this Task Contract first: node .agent-workflow/validator/validate-contract.mjs task docs/agent-tasks/ACTIVE_TASK.json
After git pull --ff-only, record exact main HEAD, branch, and pre-execution git status; refuse to overwrite unrelated dirty worktree changes.

In a disposable directory, reproduce the published @ran-sh/dsh-crew@0.3.0 default npm install failure with the normal npm resolver and capture the non-secret ERESOLVE dependency graph/root conflict. Do not use resolver bypass flags.

Inspect authoritative public npm manifests/dist-tags for the implicated @deepseek-ai packages and the currently supported official @deepseek-ai/dsh release cohort. Record exact versions/ranges used to determine the root cause; do not infer compatibility only from local lockfiles.

Implement the minimal semantically correct peer-dependency/package metadata fix. Do not solve the problem by weakening all peers to wildcard ranges or by adding install-time resolver bypasses. If peerDependenciesMeta optionality or range changes are used, document why they match the actual host/runtime contract.
Prepare v0.3.1 consistently: package.json version, src/runtime-identity.mjs runtime identity, and CHANGELOG.md must all identify 0.3.1 and describe the default-install compatibility fix.

Add or extend an automated regression test/script that builds or packs the candidate as needed and proves a fresh plain npm install of the candidate tarball succeeds with the default npm resolver in a disposable directory, with no --legacy-peer-deps, --force, --omit=peer, or equivalent bypass.

Also validate the candidate in a disposable normal-resolver install alongside the currently supported official @deepseek-ai/dsh release cohort when that is materially distinct from the standalone candidate install; record the exact host version tested.

Run pnpm install --frozen-lockfile after the dependency metadata/lockfile update is complete; if the repository workflow requires regenerating the lock first, regenerate only through pnpm and then verify frozen install succeeds.
Run the full deterministic sweep: node --test test/*.test.mjs
Run the client build: pnpm run build:client, then restore any tracked generated artifact if the repository workflow requires it and verify no unintended tracked diff remains.
Run npm pack --dry-run --json and audit package name/version, payload, size metadata, and absence of ACTIVE task/result/temp/secret/test-only artifacts from the publish payload.
Run git diff --check and record final git status; only allowed implementation files, the Result Contract, and ACTIVE task deletion may remain for completion.

Write schema_version 2 Result Contract to docs/agent-results/TASK-V031-INSTALL-COMPAT-REMEDIATION-result.json with explicit root-cause evidence, before/after install evidence, exact supported DSH cohort tested, and an overall conclusion of V031_READY or BLOCKED.

Stamp and revalidate the result: node .agent-workflow/validator/validate-contract.mjs result docs/agent-results/TASK-V031-INSTALL-COMPAT-REMEDIATION-result.json --stamp, then validate the stamped result again before completion commit.
acceptance_criteria: The published v0.3.0 ERESOLVE is reproduced and its actual peer/dependency root cause is identified from authoritative package manifests.
The fix is minimal and reflects the real dsh-crew host/runtime dependency contract rather than suppressing npm's resolver or broadly wildcarding dependency versions.
A fresh plain npm install of the packed v0.3.1 candidate succeeds with the default npm resolver and no resolver-bypass flags.
The v0.3.1 candidate is also compatible with the explicitly recorded currently supported official @deepseek-ai/dsh release cohort in a disposable normal-resolver install when applicable.
package.json, src/runtime-identity.mjs, and CHANGELOG.md consistently identify v0.3.1.
pnpm frozen install, full deterministic tests, client build, npm pack dry-run/payload audit, and git diff --check all PASS; partial or skipped required checks are not converted to PASS.
No npm registry mutation, dist-tag change, tag mutation, GitHub Release mutation, credential access, or official DSH store mutation occurs.
The validator-stamped Result Contract states V031_READY only if every required remediation and validation gate passes; otherwise it states BLOCKED with exact blockers.
On real completion, ACTIVE_TASK.json is deleted and the authorized implementation changes plus Result Contract/task deletion are committed and pushed according to the workflow.
